summary: The Attorney General runs the state Department of Justice: the state's lawyer in court, the top law-enforcement officer over local prosecutors and sheriffs, and the official who sues on behalf of Californians, including against the federal government. Incumbent Democrat Rob Bonta, appointed in 2021 and elected in 2022, placed first in the June 2 primary with 56.62%; Republican Michael Gates, former Huntington Beach city attorney and former Trump Justice Department official, placed second with 37.94%.

positions.stance: Has filed or joined more than 50 lawsuits against the second Trump administration. (CalMatters voter guide)
Enforces state laws requiring cities to permit new housing, including SB 9. (CalMatters; Wikipedia)
Authored the law requiring independent state review of police shootings of unarmed people and the private-prison ban while in the Assembly. (Wikipedia)
Would prosecute violent crime, fentanyl trafficking, and organized retail theft and enforce laws 'without political favoritism'. (Ballotpedia candidate survey)
As Huntington Beach city attorney, fought state laws requiring the city to plan for more affordable housing. (CalMatters voter guide)

Defended Huntington Beach's voter-ID law against Bonta's lawsuit; at the U.S. Justice Department helped file lawsuits seeking state and county voter-registration files. (San Joaquin Valley Sun; LAist)

key_differences: Posture toward Washington: Bonta has sued the Trump administration dozens of times; Gates worked in it, in the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division in 2025.
Housing law: Bonta enforces state mandates on cities; Gates spent years litigating against them on Huntington Beach's behalf.
These two have already met in court: Bonta (with Secretary of State Weber) sued Huntington Beach over the voter-ID ordinance Gates defended.
